content_html_sanitized:
Posted December 26, 2005
Analysis by Richard Cowan

Bud Inc
By Ian Mulgrew
Random House, Canada
Available on Amazon.com

Lately, I have been so distracted by various governments trying to kill some of my friends that I have neglected to recommend a book by another friend, Ian Mulgrew.
See
 Facing January 12th Expulsion From Canada, The Kubbys Launch Legal Assault On Refugee Process. Now Is The Time For Kubby's Supporters -- And Friends Of Freedom Everywhere -- To Rally Behind Them.
and
 Steve Tuck Is A Free Man. Vindicated. Recuperating from Five Year Ordeal. Will Return to Mining Business in Canada After First Of Year.

Mulgrew, the author of several books, writes a column for the Vancouver Sun on legal affairs, illegal affairs might be more apt, so it was only appropriate that he would have a go at describing the world of BC Bud.

Here is the back-story on Marc Emery andMichelle Rainey, Advanced Nutrients and Vancouver’s short-lived Da Kine coffee shop, as well as Dutch, American and Canadian growers.

I think that readers of MarijuanaNews will find this book a very interesting way to learn more about many of the people on whom I have reported over the last few years. I certainly learned a few things myself.

Ian is a very gregarious fellow who makes no secret of his views on cannabis — he likes it - and cannabis prohibition - he doesn’t like it. Consequently, a number of people in the industry were happy to talk to him, probably a bit too candidly, but that certainly makes the book more informative.

Ian and I met in Vancouver while he was doing research for the book, and, as he describes in the last chapter, we ended up in Amsterdam together for the 2004 Cannabis Cup. I introduced him to some of my Dutch friends, like Nol van Schaik, and his insights into the Dutch scene are a bonus.
See
 Beyond The Cannabis Cup: A Few Things You Should Not Overlook In Amsterdam.
and
 Two BC Growers Bag Cannabis Cup Prizes. Dutch Growers Face Competition and Government Harassment. Spain Looks Warmer. Reporting from Amsterdam.

He begins the book with a conversation with a Vancouver economist, Stephen Easton, who has estimated that the BC cannabis industry may be as large as $7 billion per year. Although the books subtitle is -Inside Canada’s Marijuana Industry, the booming trade in Ontario and Quebec is not included in that $7 billion.  

Canadian narks like to use the highest estimates when they are seeking more money and power, in order to make the problem seem as large as possible. The absurdity of trying to eliminate what would be one of the province’s largest industries seems to be lost on the prohibitionists... like so much else.
See
 Time Magazine Reports BC Bud 20% Less Potent Than Four Years Ago?? Incompetent Prohibitionist Propaganda and Even Worse Journalism. As Some Reporters Die to Find the Truth Others Live to Lie.
and links

On the other hand, the industry’s own boosters also like to make it sound important, but that can backfire. Ask Marc Emery. Of course, no one really knows the size of contraband markets, and the same problem applies to the individual players. Do they really do the dollar volume that they claim? There is no way to be sure.

My problem with the higher estimates has always been in trying to figure out where it all goes. The prohibitionists like to claim that as much as 90% of BC Bud goes to the US, but whatever the real export numbers may be, seizures at the US/Canadian border are only about 2% of the volume at the Mexican border, and I just cannot believe that they are missing so much on the Northern border.  

Moreover, until a few years ago, the most common way of smuggling BC Bud was in hockey bags (about 70 pounds), and there is no way that billions were taken south that way. And if so many billions of dollars of Canadian bud really is sold in the US, then the total US market must be vastly bigger than most estimates. But that is entirely possible.

None of this is Mulgrew’s problem. He just describes the history, the components and players. He does that very well, so anyone who wants to understand a major part of the contemporary cannabis world needs to read Bud Inc. Fortunately, that is also a good way to spend a weekend.
